subject: Entry surface per-cloud + fallback policy — decision log
messages:
From: Alicia Zhang <azhang@cloudmarketplace.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael O'Rourke <michael.orourke@partnercloud.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: CloudLogic listing — initial coverage matrix + ask

Marissa / Ben — thanks for the quick intro last week. As we prep the AWS/Azure/GCP co-sell decks, attached is a first-pass coverage matrix showing where CloudLogic wants to feature Redwood (managed inference, private deployments, dedicated pools). High level asks:

- Confirm which SKUs we can list per cloud (entry surface): hosted API, dedicated reserved, private VPC package.
- Desired regions: us-east-1, us-west-2 for AWS; westeurope for Azure; us-central1 for GCP initially.
- Fallback policy: if dedicated capacity is unavailable in a region, can we auto-route to hosted API under a specific SLA?

We'd like a short decision log and a recommended default mapping we can include in the partner submission by 11/10. Attachment: redwood_cloudlogic_coverage_matrix_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Thanks,
Alicia
Partnerships, Cloud Marketplace
CloudMarketPlace.io
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Zhang <azhang@cloudmarketplace.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CloudLogic listing — initial coverage matrix + ask

Alicia — thanks for the matrix, helpful. Looping in Ben and Vanessa for SKU and marketplace ops input. High-level response below; we should align on a canonical mapping and a simple fallback rule.

- Entry surface (recommended defaults):
  * AWS: Hosted API (all customers), Dedicated Reserved (enterprise customers only), Private (VPC/on-prem for regulated customers).
  * Azure: Hosted API + Dedicated Reserved in regions where we can provision GPUs (westeurope initially).
  * GCP: Hosted API + Private (for customers wanting GCP-native VPC); Dedicated is limited for GCP for now.

- Regions: agree with your starter set, but we should add us-west-1 (latency-sensitive customers on the West Coast) as a conditional for AWS.

- Fallback policy (proposal): route to the next compatible offering in this order: Dedicated -> Private (same region) -> Hosted API (closest region). Requests marked as "compliant-only" for Private must not route to Hosted API. We'll need a toggle per listing to indicate whether fallback to Hosted is allowed.

Can you share the partner submission deadline again? We'll aim to provide a decision table by EOD Friday.

—Marissa
Director, Cloud GTM
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: CloudLogic listing — initial coverage matrix + ask

On Mon, Nov 2, 2026 at 9:15 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> - Entry surface (recommended defaults):
>   * AWS: Hosted API (all customers), Dedicated Reserved (enterprise customers only), Private (VPC/on-prem for regulated customers).

Quick notes from marketplace ops and SKU team:
1) SKU granularity — we should avoid gating by customer size in the listing metadata. Instead publish three SKUs per cloud: hosted-api, reserved-dedicated, private-vpc. Enrollment rules (which customers qualify) are enforced in our partner portal and deal workflow, not the listing.
2) Region availability matrix — dedicated SKUs will be marked as "availability: limited" with a pointer to allowed zones. We'll maintain a dynamic fallback-config file that marketplace integrators can call.
3) Billing note — for dedicated reserved we need the contract term (monthly/annual) to appear in the SKU description, CloudMarketPlace prefers a single line in the listing that references a contract page rather than lengthy terms.

I'll draft the canonical SKU names and a JSON snippet for the fallback policy. Vanessa / Karthik, any red flags on Azure / GCP coverage?

—Ben
Sr. Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: CloudLogic listing — initial coverage matrix + ask

Thanks Ben — quick additions from channel/marketplace listing side:
- Azure SKU naming needs to include "region-tag" for the marketplace metadata (westeurope -> WEU).
- GCP: because of partner marketplace constraints, we should mark the dedicated SKU as "pilot" and limit to invited accounts until we have orchestration in place. Public listing should show Hosted + Private only.
- Canary package: propose a 30-day canary in us-east-1 (AWS) and westeurope (Azure). If telemetries (latency/error rate) remain within thresholds, flip the dedicated SKU to wide availability.

Action items I took: created a shared folder with the draft coverage matrix and a short one-pager for CloudLogic: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bCoverageMatrix (see proposal_summary_CloudLogic.pdf)

Vanessa

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Final — CloudLogic listing mapping + canonical fallback policy (for partner submission)

Alicia / Michael — thanks for the patience. Below is the consolidated decision log and the canonical mappings we'll publish with the partner submission on your side. We've attached the final coverage matrix for reference.

Final mapping (short):
- AWS: SKUs = redwood-hosted, redwood-dedicated-reserved, redwood-private-vpc. Regions: us-east-1 (canary), us-west-2, us-west-1 (conditional). Dedicated = limited availability on launch.
- Azure: SKUs = redwood-hosted, redwood-dedicated-reserved (WEU pilot), redwood-private-vpc. Regions: westeurope (WEU) primary.
- GCP: SKUs = redwood-hosted, redwood-private-vpc. Dedicated = pilot/invite-only. Region: us-central1 primary.

Canonical fallback rule (simple):
1) If requested SKU unavailable in same-region dedicated pool -> route to private-vpc in same region (if customer allowed).
2) If private-vpc not allowed or unavailable -> route to hosted API in nearest region (respecting data residency flags).
3) If request has "no-hosted-fallback" flag -> failover only to other customer-owned private endpoints; return 409 and partner-supplied instructions if none available.

Open items for partner submission:
- Confirm CloudLogic accepts our canary plan (30 days in us-east-1 & westeurope).
- Which CloudLogic customer segments should we mark as "invite-only" for dedicated pilot? (suggest: enterprise accounts > $250k ARR).

Attached: redwood_cloudlogic_coverage_matrix_v1.xlsx, proposal_summary_CloudLogic.pdf
Related reference: HS-789234 (HubSpot).

If this looks good, we'll send a slimmed one-pager for the partner portal by Monday.

—Marissa
Director, Cloud GTM
